findings.title: Throw presets say even all-out breaks no windows while the air takes megatons from the car in flight; the 'upper bound' label is false
findings.location: src/engine.js RESTRAINT.MOVES.throw.blast (counts only a supersonic landing or a fireball at 1% of c); app.html PRESET_WHAT.windows/houses/block and the 'Even all-out, this move doesn't …' note in resolveEffort
findings.evidence: Dial 10^15 kg (logKg 15), Throw, car, 45°, concrete, effort 'Break windows across the street'. The page says: 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t break windows 15 m from where it lands, across a street (if all the energy went into the air: an upper bound).' 'Level a block' says: 'doesn’t flatten houses 100 m from where it lands'. The tiles on the same view: 'Energy in the car 5.83 PJ | 1.4 Mt TNT', 'Lands at 46.6 m/s | 350 g TNT on impact', chip 'Air heating: 360 million °C at the nose', 'Rex gets shoved backward at 592 km/s'. The hazard list has no air-blast line at all. claims/t_throw15.js: launch 2,949 km/s (0.98% of c, so not treated as a fireball). Drag loss 1.39 Mt TNT. Rex's recoil carries 126 kt. MOVES.throw.blast returns 0. Fed to the page's own blastRadius, the drag loss gives 6.9 kPa out to 15 km and 26.8 kPa out to 5.9 km. claims/t_throw2.js: at 10^9, 10^12 and 10^15 kg the windows, houses and block presets all come out 'never'. At 10^18 kg (≥1% c) they fire at once. At 10^9 kg the drag loss is already 1.4 t TNT.
findings.expected: Air drag turns almost all of the object's kinetic energy into hot, shocked air along its first km. The page's own card rule is that a blast counts when something moves past Mach 1, and here the car does. It should not claim no window damage under an 'upper bound' label. Rex's own Mach-1,700 recoil is also energy dumped into the air.
findings.fix: In MOVES.throw.blast, add the flight's drag loss when the launch is supersonic: shock(r.v, r.dragLoss), with the energy placed at the thrower or along the path. Add Rex's recoil energy when recoilV ≥ a0. Failing that, make the 'never' text say: 'the lab counts only the landing; the X t TNT the air takes in flight is not counted.'

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh build (scratch v/t1.js in the browser, v/t_throw.js in Node). Settings: logKg 15, Throw, car, 45°, concrete, preset 'Break windows across the street'. The page says: 'The car flies 1.58 km… Launch: 2,950 km/s… Even all-out, this move doesn’t break windows 15 m from where it lands, across a street (if all the energy went into the air: an upper bound).' The hazard list has no air-blast line. In the engine, MOVES.throw.blast(r) = 0 (v = 0.984% of c, so not 'relativistic'; landing at 46.6 m/s is subsonic). r.dragLoss = Eobj = 1.39 Mt TNT. Fed to the page's own blastRadius, that is 6.9 kPa out to 15.0 km, 26.8 kPa out to 5.86 km and 100 Pa out to 936 km. At logKg 12: drag loss 1.39 kt, 6.9 kPa out to 1.5 km, and the car lands 1.17 km away. At 9, 12 and 15 the windows, houses and block presets all come out 'never'. Rex's recoil kinetic energy is 126 kt TNT at 10^15. The energy counted is only the landing's (0.35 kg TNT), so 'if all the energy went into the air: an upper bound' is false. The air drag deposits the car's whole energy along its path, which ends at the landing site. The courtesy ceiling is unaffected, because the boom hazard fires first, but the not-so-heroic presets and their 'never' text are wrong for every supersonic throw below 1% of c.
verdict.better_fix: engine.js MOVES.throw: count the flight's drag loss as a shock when the launch is supersonic, and the recoil when it is: blast: (r) => (!r.canMove || !r.flight ? 0 : r.flight.relativistic ? r.Eobj : shock(r.v, r.dragLoss != null ? r.dragLoss : r.Eobj) + (r.flight.landed ? shock(r.flight.vImpact, r.Eimpact) : 0) + shock(r.recoilV || 0, 0.5 * r.mA * r.recoilV * r.recoilV)). Here mA stands for Rex's mass in the result. This places the energy at the landing, which keeps it an upper bound. Where M.where is 'where it lands', change the distance wording to 'from its path' when r.v ≥ a0. Failing that, add to the never-note when r.v ≥ a0: ' This counts only the landing; the ' + fmtTNT(r.dragLoss) + ' the air takes from it in flight is not counted.'

outcome.change: MOVES.throw.blast counts a launch past Mach 1: the energy the air takes in flight (none with Cool flight) plus his recoil past Mach 1, as a blast from him; the larger of that and the landing counts. A car at 10^15 kg now sets the windows preset.

findings.title: Sprint, Pull, Punch and Clap claim no ground shaking or rattling, but they have no shaking model, and the Walk tab contradicts them
findings.location: engine.js RESTRAINT.MOVES.sprint/pull/punch/clap (no shake); app.html effortReadout 'Hazards checked' text, the 'Courtesy ceiling: none…' line and the preset 'never' text
findings.evidence: Sand, default strength, Sprint, preset 'Rattle the windows': 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t rattle windows and ornaments 5 m away, through the ground or the air.' Also: 'Courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing this move does harms anyone 5 m or more away, even all-out.' (top speed 41.7 m/s). Pull on sand, all-out (10 m in 2.27 s), gives the same rattle text. The 'Hazards checked' text lists 'ground shaking that may crack plaster' as checked. On the Walk tab on sand, Rex walking at an ordinary step gives 'Windows and ornaments rattle (1 mm/s): out to 8.48 m'. Stamping steps give 'Plaster may crack (7.6 mm/s): out to 9.32 m' (claims/walk1.txt; claims/t_walk.js: ordinary 1.58 mm/s at 5 m). Running footfalls (2–2.9× weight, the Weight tab's own figure) lie between an ordinary step and a stamp. README Known limits: 'Running steps (Sprint) are not checked for ground shaking.' The page never says this. Punch at 10^12 kg, plaster preset: 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t shake the ground enough that plaster may crack 5 m away' in the same readout as 'could flatten houses 100 m away'. Clap at 10^12 kg: the same text with 250 t TNT released.
findings.expected: With no shaking model, the page cannot assert that the move doesn't shake the ground. The Walk tab's own numbers show that a 3-tonne walker on sand rattles windows past 5 m.
findings.fix: When MOVES[move].shake is undefined, write 'The lab doesn’t model ground shaking for this move' in the preset never-text, in the 'Hazards checked' list and in the ceiling line, and print the README limit on the page. Better: give Sprint and Pull a step source (walkStep with a running load).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v/t2.js). On sand at default strength, Sprint with preset 'Rattle the windows' says: 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t rattle windows and ornaments 5 m away, through the ground or the air.' It also says: 'Courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing this move does harms anyone 5 m or more away, even all-out.' The 'Hazards checked' text lists 'ground shaking that may crack plaster' as checked. Pull on sand all-out (10 m in 2.27 s) gives the same rattle sentence. In the engine, MOVES.sprint/pull/punch/clap.shake are all undefined, so the rattle and plaster preset tests are always false. The Walk model gives Rex's ordinary walking step on sand 1.58 mm/s at 5 m (rattle reach 8.48 m; stamp 11.8 mm/s, plaster reach 9.32 m), and the page's own sprint text puts each stride at about 2.5× his weight. The page therefore asserts as fact something its own model contradicts. Punch at 10^12 kg with the plaster preset: 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t shake the ground enough that plaster may crack 5 m away.' The same readout says it 'could flatten houses 100 m away' (150 t TNT). Clap at 10^12 kg is the same (250 t TNT). The only disclaimer is in the README ('Running steps (Sprint) are not checked for ground shaking'). A grep finds none on the page except the Walk tab's unmodelled-surface line.
verdict.better_fix: app.html resolveEffort, never branch: if ((e === 'rattle' || e === 'plaster') && !P.RESTRAINT.MOVES[move].shake) out.note = 'The lab doesn’t model ground shaking for this move' + (e === 'rattle' && P.RESTRAINT.MOVES[move].blast ? ' (only the air blast is checked, and even all-out it doesn’t rattle windows ' + fmtDist(state.near) + ' away)' : '') + ', so it can’t say.'; else keep the current text. In effortReadout, when !M.shake, change 'Nothing this move does harms anyone' to 'Nothing the lab checks for this move harms anyone', and replace the 'Hazards checked' paragraph with one built from the hazards the move defines, adding 'Ground shaking isn’t modelled for this move.' Later: give Sprint and Pull a step source from walkStep with a running load (k ≈ 2.5).

outcome.change: For Sprint, Pull, Punch and Clap the page says the lab doesn't model their ground shaking (ceiling line, hazard list, rattle and plaster presets).

findings.title: In soil, red 'Ground gives' chips sit beside readouts saying the ground doesn't break and nothing is harmed
findings.location: app.html bayThrow chip 'Ground gives way under his feet', bayJump gchip 'Ground gives: feet sink …', stomp hole tile; engine MOVES.throw/jump/stomp ground() soil rule
findings.evidence: Sand, default strength, Throw (car), least disruptive: chips 'Footing: feet slide, he recoils · Ground gives way under his feet'; readout 'The most he can do with nothing nearby harmed.' With preset 'Break the ground under him' the same chip shows next to 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t break the ground under his feet.' Jump on sand, default: 'Rex jumps 1.13 m high and leaves two deep footprints', chip 'Ground gives: feet sink 68 cm', with 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t break the ground under his feet.' Jump on sand at 10^12 kg, least: chip 'Ground gives: feet sink 68 cm', but the readout says 'past lifting 225 t the ground under his feet gives way'. At 227 t the verdict flips to 'leaves two craters behind' with the same 68 cm sink. Stomp on sand, all-out: 'Hole under his foot 61 cm deep' with 'doesn’t break the ground under his feet'. The soil rule ('only a crater counts') is in the README only. Nothing on the page says it (grep finds none).
findings.expected: The chip and the readout should use one definition. In soil, sinking is treated as a footprint and only more than 1 MJ into the ground counts as a crater, so the chips should not say the ground gives way, or the readout should explain the rule.
findings.fix: In soil, label the chip 'Feet sink 68 cm (footprints, not broken ground)'. Word the soil hazard and the 'ground' preset as 'he leaves craters (over 1 MJ into the ground)'. Add one line or card sentence stating the soil rule.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v/t3.js). Sand, default strength, Throw (car), least disruptive: chips 'Footing: feet slide, he recoils · Ground gives way under his feet' sit beside 'The most he can do with nothing nearby harmed.' With preset 'Break the ground under him', the same red chip sits beside 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t break the ground under his feet.' Jump on sand with the ground preset: chip 'Ground gives: feet sink 68 cm' and 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t break the ground under his feet.' Jump on sand at 10^12 kg, least: chip 'Ground gives: feet sink 68 cm', then 'past lifting 225 t the ground under his feet gives way'. Stomp on sand with the ground preset: 'Hole under his foot 61 cm deep' and 'doesn’t break the ground under his feet.' The engine's soil rule (MOVES.*.ground returns false in SOIL unless more than 1 MJ makes a crater) uses the same words (EFF_HAZ.ground.what = 'the ground under his feet gives way') as the chips (app.html 1261, 1374), which fire on sinkRatio > 1 or groundFails. A grep finds no page text stating the soil rule; only the README has it. These are adjacent statements that contradict each other on a common surface choice.
verdict.better_fix: Use one definition and say it. (1) In soil, word the chips as footprints: app.html 1261: chips.push(SOIL.has(c.surface.id) ? status('warn', 'Feet sink in (footprints, not broken ground)') : status('bad', 'Ground gives way under his feet')). 1374: gchip = status(soil ? 'warn' : 'bad', (soil ? 'Feet sink ' : 'Ground gives: feet sink ') + fmtDist(r.sink) + (soil ? ' (footprints)' : '')). (2) In soil, have EFF_HAZ.ground.what and PRESET_WHAT.ground say 'he leaves a crater (over 1 MJ into the ground; in soil, sinking in is only a footprint)'. (3) Add that sentence to the courtesy-ceiling card in static-data.js.

outcome.change: In soil the Throw and Jump chips say the feet sink in (footprints); the hazard and preset say 'leaves craters' and state the 1 MJ line for a jump.

findings.title: Jump: the air blast is counted because the feet pass Mach 1, but the same list says there is no sonic boom
findings.location: engine.js MOVES.jump: blast = shock(r.footSpeed, …) but speed = r.v (body) for the boom hazard
findings.evidence: Dial 10^12 kg, Jump, concrete, preset 'Break windows across the street' (26,900 t): 'Rex jumps 485 m high and leaves two craters behind', chip 'Ground gives: feet sink 65 cm' (no boom chip). The list reads: 'Sonic boom from 0.031% (lifting 310,000 t); not now.' and 'Air blast loud enough to risk damage at 5 m from lifting 27,000 t; now out to 2.52 km from him.' claims/t_jump2.js: at 26,872 t footSpeed = 340 m/s and body speed = 101 m/s. The boom test is false and the air test true. The boom hazard is defined as 'something he moves, or he himself, breaks the sound barrier'.
findings.expected: The lab's rule is that an air blast exists only because something moved past Mach 1, so that same movement is a sonic boom. The two lines contradict each other.
findings.fix: Give MOVES.jump boomSpeed: (r) => Math.max(r.v, r.footSpeed || 0), as the stomp does with vFoot.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced (v/t6.js). logKg 12, Jump, concrete, preset 'Break windows across the street' (26,900 t): no boom chip. The list says 'Sonic boom from 0.031% (lifting 310,000 t); not now.' and 'Air blast loud enough to risk damage at 5 m from lifting 27,000 t; now out to 2.52 km from him.' The page also says 'His feet punch 65 cm into the ground at up to 340 m/s.' In the engine at that effort, footSpeed = 340.4 m/s (≥ a0) and body v = 101 m/s. MOVES.jump.blast = shock(r.footSpeed, Eground), but the boom uses speed = r.v. By the page's own definitions ('something he moves… breaks the sound barrier'; a blast only when something passes Mach 1), the two lines contradict each other. The stomp uses vFoot for both.
verdict.better_fix: engine.js MOVES.jump: add boomSpeed: (r) => Math.max(r.v, r.footSpeed || 0), (as the stomp does with vFoot).

outcome.change: MOVES.jump.boomSpeed counts his feet (max of body and foot speed).

findings.evidence: peek.js, Jump, ∞ chip, effort 'Courtesy ceiling': 'Effort: as hard as lifting 134 t. The most he can use before something nearby comes to harm.' / 'Courtesy ceiling: lifting 130 t. verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced in the browser (vcode/drive.js). Jump, ∞, effort 'Courtesy ceiling':
- 'Effort: as hard as lifting 134 t. The most he can use before something nearby comes to harm.'
- 'Courtesy ceiling: lifting 130 t. Past that, the ground shakes hard enough that plaster may crack 5 m away.'
